decoded.meaning: FWD{ op=REPLY, dst=/reply-ep, src=<path label 0:1>/sensor, kind=ERROR, STATUS{ ERROR{ VALUE u16=0x0020 tr::path::not_found } } } - what acl/label-vs-string-allow's frame answers when the caller is NOT allowed.
decoded.note: The refusal is tr::path::not_found and NOT tr::access::denied, deliberately: RFC-0027 8.1's anti-enumeration property requires a labelled probe to yield what a string probe yields, never `exists + here is a handle to it`. Answering `denied` would confirm the label is live, so a denied label and a stale one are made indistinguishable. The reply's src echoes the refused spelling so the sender can correlate it and fall back to the full-string path it still holds (7.2).
